title: Rethinking Data Augmentation for Single-Source Domain Generalization in Medical Image Segmentation (SLAug)
mechanism: Global plus class-wise random Bezier intensity curves (location-scale per class region), fused via a gradient saliency map so augmentation targets regions the model relies on.
adaptation: Apply class-wise curves only to structural classes (busbar, ribbon, gridline, border, background, padding, frame); never to crack or inactive, because a class-wise transform on 1 px jittered labels paints a line at the label rather than the dark ridge and creates a shortcut. Forces crack detection under any busbar/background contrast, which CSIR half-cuts change.
min_experiment: PF + SLAug (crack/inactive excluded) vs PF, 3 seeds. E1 crack relF1@2 primary, test crack IoU and mIoU_rob guard. Kill if E1 gain < +0.03 or test crack IoU drops > 0.01.
evidence: R: exceeds prior SDG methods by a large margin on two medical SDG tasks (abstract; numbers not read). Code public.
prior_overlap: none: no class-wise or non-linear intensity augmentation was run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Class-wise curves only on structural classes (busbar, ribbons, border, frame_edge, gridline, sp_mono/sp_multi, background); keep crack and inactive darker than their neighbours. Mimics source contrast conventions and new module types.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+SLAug vs PF+GIN-IPA and PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill: < +0.02 E1 relF1@2 over GIN-IPA.
